chapters.summary: On the eve of Rama's coronation, Kaikeyi claims her two boons. Rama accepts exile without a word of complaint. Sumitra blesses Lakshmana, Guha ferries them over the Ganga, and at Chitrakuta Bharata takes Rama's sandals to rule in his name.

signs.text: Ayodhya, the unconquerable city of the Ikshvaku kings.
The school of the sage Vasishtha, family priest of the Ikshvakus.
Shringaverapura, town of Guha, king of the Nishadas. The ford of the Ganga.
South: the great forest of Dandaka.

then.say: Ayodhya, city of the Ikshvaku kings. Twelve happy years have passed since Rama and Sita were married.
King Dasharatha has grown old. With the joyful consent of his people, he has chosen Rama as his heir. The coronation is tomorrow.
Banners fly from every roof. The streets are sprinkled with water and strewn with flowers.
{player}, look at the city! Everyone is singing my brother's name.

then.objective: Go to the palace at the north end of the city.

then.say: The gate is open. May the gods go with the princes.
Rama is to leave the city. But first he will take leave of his teacher Vasishtha, at the school in the west.

else.say: Welcome to Ayodhya! The coronation is tomorrow. The whole city is celebrating.

then.say: Not yet, friend. Rama will take leave of his teacher Vasishtha first. The school is in the west of the city.

then.objective: Go to Vasishtha's school in the west of the city.

else.say: Leave the city now? The coronation is tomorrow! Go and see the palace.

then.say: I am to drive the princes and Sita to the edge of the kingdom. Never has a charioteer had a sadder task.

else.say: I am Sumantra, the king's charioteer and minister. The king has summoned Rama to the palace.

then.say: Rama has come to take leave of his teacher. Go in.

else.say: The scholars are busy composing hymns for the coronation.

then.say: Rama will come here to take leave of his teacher. But Lakshmana has not yet taken leave of his mother, Queen Sumitra. Visit her in the palace first.

then.objective: Speak with Queen Sumitra in the palace.

else.say: The school is closed today, friend. The scholars are preparing hymns for the coronation.

then.say: There is weeping in the palace today.

else.say: Go in. The king is expecting the princes.

cmds.say: The royal hall of the Ikshvakus. Walk softly.
This shrine is open to all. Rest here, save your journey, or recite the verses you have heard.

then.say: Beautiful. Let it be known: Rama is Dasharatha, Sita is the mother, and the forest is Ayodhya.

else.say: The blessing is whole. May it guard the princes in the forest.
You carry Queen Sumitra's blessing to her son. Will you recite it here, so that it is whole again?

then.say: Beautiful. Let it be known: Rama is Dasharatha, Sita is the mother, and the forest is Ayodhya.

else.say: Almost. Some words are still out of place. Try again when you are ready.
As you wish.

cmds.say: Fruit and roots, fresh from the royal gardens! Stock up, traveller.
Healing herbs from the Himalaya, and honey from the forests of the south.

then.say: Rama to the forest for fourteen years? The city is like a night without a moon.

else.say: Rama will be crowned! He greets every one of us by name, you know, even a poor man like me.

then.say: Even the elephants will not eat today. Everyone weeps for Rama.

else.say: I have made a garland of jasmine for the coronation. Is it not lovely?

cmds.say: The market of Ayodhya has everything. If your heroes are weary, buy fruit. If their mantras run dry, buy honey.

then.say: Why is everyone crying? Mother says Rama is going away.

then.choice: The child asks you: "Why is Rama going away?"

then.say: To the forest? But why?
Fourteen years! But why is he going?
Then Rama keeps his word, even when it is hard. I will keep mine too!

else.say: I climbed the wall to see the decorations! There are lamps all along the royal road.

then.say: I have put my loom away. How could anyone weave for a feast today?
My neighbour serves in the palace. She says Rama told Queen Kaikeyi: 'Tell me what the king wishes, and I will do it. Rama does not speak twice.'
{w:dvis} means "twice". Rama gives his word once, and keeps it, whatever it costs him.

else.say: I am weaving cloth for the coronation feast. Have you ever seen silk so fine?

cmds.say: In my youth I saw King Dasharatha ride out to help the gods in battle. Queen Kaikeyi drove his chariot and saved his life that day.
He promised her two boons for it. She never asked for them. I wonder if she ever will.
Every pot I make, I give one to the hermitages. A small gift, given gladly, is a great gift.

then.say: The potter gives you 2 fruits.

cmds.say: But in the night, everything changed.
Queen Kaikeyi, stirred up by her maid Manthara, reminded the king of the two boons he had promised her long ago, when she saved his life in battle.
She asked that her son Bharata be crowned instead, and that Rama live in the forest for fourteen years.
Bound by his word, the old king wept. When Rama came to him in the morning, he could not bring himself to speak.
Rama...
Rama, the king once promised me two boons. He cannot bear to tell you himself. Will you do what he wishes?
Mother, tell me what the king desires, and I will do it. I give you my word.
Kaikeyi tells him of the boons: Bharata will be crowned, and Rama must live in the forest for fourteen years.
So be it. I will go to the forest this very day. I do not care for the kingdom.

onCorrect.say: Yes. My brother never speaks {w:dvis} (twice). He never takes back his word.

onWrong.say: Not quite. The verse card shows each word. My brother never takes back his word.

cmds.say: Brother, this is unjust! How can you accept it?
Lakshmana, it is our father's word. Do not be angry with anyone. Help me keep it.
Sita will not stay behind. "Where you go, I go," she says. "With you, the forest will be my palace." Lakshmana, too, will follow his brother.

cmds.objective: Speak with Queen Sumitra, Lakshmana's mother, in the east chamber.

then.say: Rama... my son...
The old king cannot say more. He holds to his word, though it breaks his heart.

else.say: Tomorrow my Rama will be crowned.

then.say: Queen Kaikeyi stands apart, silent, her face turned away.

else.say: Welcome, children.

then.say: My son is going to the forest. I asked to go with him, but he told me my place is beside the king.
May the forest, the rivers and the mountains protect him. May every god and sage keep him safe.

else.say: I have spent the night in prayer for my son.

then.say: A wife walks with her husband, in the palace or the forest. I am not afraid of the forest. With Rama it will be like a garden.

else.say: Welcome, {player}.

then.say: Go with my blessing, my son. And you, child, keep these words safe.

else.say: Lakshmana kneels before his mother, Queen Sumitra.
My son, you were born to stand beside Rama. In good fortune or in hardship, never neglect him.
I will, mother. Rama will be my father, and Sita my mother. The forest will be my {w:ayodhya}.

onWrong.say: Look at the verse card again, child. Each word is a gift.

else.say: Child, this is the blessing I most want the world to keep. Recite it at a shrine to make it whole: the temple priest near the market will hear you.

else.objective: Go with Rama to Vasishtha's school, in the west of the city.

else.say: My sons Lakshmana and Shatrughna love their brothers more than themselves.

cmds.say: A student of Valmiki? Then answer me this: why should a prince give up a kingdom for a promise someone else made? Defend your view!

battle.intro: A scholar of Vasishtha's school challenges you to a debate!

onWin.say: I am persuaded. A promise kept is the root of all trust. Go on.

onWin.objective: Debate the next scholar, further into the hall.

cmds.say: I am persuaded. A promise kept is the root of all trust. Go on.
Anger at injustice is natural. Should Lakshmana not be angry today? Prove me wrong!

battle.intro: A scholar of Vasishtha's school challenges you to a debate!

onWin.say: Persuaded. Rama's calm is a greater strength than anger. The teacher waits beyond.

onWin.objective: Debate the last scholar, near the head of the hall.

cmds.say: Persuaded. Rama's calm is a greater strength than anger. The teacher waits beyond.
I am the last of Vasishtha's students. Tell me: what dharma is greater than serving one's father?

battle.intro: A scholar of Vasishtha's school challenges you to a debate!

onWin.say: None, as Rama himself said. You have heard the verses well. Go to our teacher.

onWin.objective: Speak with the sage Vasishtha at the head of the hall.

cmds.say: None, as Rama himself said. You have heard the verses well. Go to our teacher.

then.say: {w:dharma} (righteousness) protects those who protect it. Go well, children.
My students are persuaded, and so am I. You understand what Rama is doing: holding to truth, even at a terrible cost.
Rama, go with my blessing. Fourteen years will pass, and you will come home.
Teacher, look after my father and my mothers.
Vasishtha gives you 2 healing herbs.

then.objective: Leave Ayodhya by the south gate.

else.say: So you are the student of Valmiki. Rama has come to take leave of me, and you have come to learn.
Debate my three students. Each has a question about what you heard today. Persuade them all, then come to me.

else.objective: Persuade the three scholars of Vasishtha's school.

then.say: In a debate, your conviction is your strength. Answer well and you shake the other side's conviction. Persuade them, and the debate is won!
If the questions come too fast, turn on Relaxed in the menu's Settings. Then there is no time limit at all.
In a debate, your conviction is your strength. Recite well and you shake the other side's conviction. Persuade them, and the debate is won!
On this journey there is no need to be quick: recite at your own pace. Want more practice? Every shrine has a study hall.
Dressed in bark, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana leave Ayodhya in Sumantra's chariot. The whole city weeps and runs after them.
On the first night they rest on the bank of the Tamasa, and before dawn they slip away, so that the people will go home.
The Tamasa! The very river where the first verse was born. You feel the poem folding back on itself.
At last they reach the Ganga, at Shringaverapura, the town of Guha, king of the Nishadas.

then.objective: Find Guha, king of the Nishadas, at the river.

then.say: My boat is yours whenever you wish to cross, friends. Just walk down to the steps.
Rama, my dear friend! This land is yours. Stay and rule here, and let me serve you.
Guha, I have vowed to live as a hermit in the forest. Your love is gift enough.

then.choice: Guha turns to you: "And you, young friend? Where are you going?"

options.label: I am a student of Valmiki.

then.say: From Ayodhya, yes. But where are you going now?
A student of a great sage! But tell me, where are you going?
Then you are Rama's friend, and mine too.
That night Guha and Lakshmana keep watch together, speaking of Rama until dawn.
In the morning Rama sends Sumantra home with gentle words for the king.
My boat is ready. Let me take you across the Ganga.
Guha's boatmen row them across the wide, shining Ganga.
On the far bank, the sage Bharadvaja of Prayaga welcomes them and shows them the way to the hill of Chitrakuta.

else.say: Welcome, traveller.

cmds.say: The ferry is Guha's to command, friend. Speak with him first.
The Ganga is wide here, but our boats are strong. Guha's people know every current.
Honey from the hives, roots from the hills. Trade with the Nishadas!
Our king Guha loves Rama like a brother. When he heard Rama was coming, he ran all the way to the river.
Wolves come out of the tall grass at dusk. Mother says to walk on the path!

then.say: Chitrakuta: a green hill of flowering trees above the Mandakini river. Lakshmana builds a hut of leaves, and for a while the three live happily.
Sita, see the Mandakini, bright with lotuses. Living here with you and Lakshmana, I do not miss the kingdom at all.
Nor do I. The forest has been kind to us.

then.objective: Go to the leaf hut by the river.

then.say: Bharata is a good brother. It hurt Rama to send him away.

else.say: Someone is coming up the hill. Look, there by the hut!

then.say: I will keep the sandals safe, brother.

else.say: A great host approaches. Lakshmana fears an attack, but it is Bharata, on foot, in bark cloth, weeping.
King Dasharatha has died of grief. Bharata has refused the throne and has come to bring his brother home.
Brother, the kingdom is yours. I will never take it. Come back to Ayodhya!
Bharata, our father's word must stand. I will return when the fourteen years are over. Rule for the people until then.
At last Bharata asks for Rama's sandals. "I will set them on the throne," he says, "and rule as their servant, living as a hermit until you return."
Bharata places the sandals on his head and goes back to Ayodhya.

then.objective: Meet the challenger at the south path.

else.objective: Restore Sumitra's verse with Valmiki at the shrine, then go to the south path.

cmds.say: {player}! Yes, this is my own hermitage, inside my own poem. Rama comes here in the story, just as you have.

then.say: Whole again. Lakshmana's new mantra comes from it: the word that means "know this!"

then.objective: Meet Bharadvaja on the south path.

else.say: Go on, {player}. Bharadvaja is waiting on the south path.
You heard Queen Sumitra's blessing. Recite it for me here, by the shrine, and make it whole.

then.say: Whole again. Lakshmana's new mantra comes from it: the word that means "know this!"

then.objective: Meet Bharadvaja on the south path.

else.say: Not quite whole yet. Look at the verse card again, then recite it for me once more.
When you are ready, then.
Rest here whenever you need to.

then.say: {player}! The teacher sent me to see how you are doing. But look: a great crowd is coming up the hill. Go and see; we can debate later.
Not so fast! Queen Sumitra's blessing is still scattered. Restore it first, with the teacher at the shrine by his hut, in the west.

then.objective: Restore Sumitra's verse with Valmiki at the shrine.

else.say: A great sage of Prayaga shares my name, so I must live up to it! The teacher sent me to test you once more.
Our first debate was practice. This time I will not hold back!

battle.intro: Bharadvaja challenges you to a verse-debate!

onWin.say: Persuaded again! You know these verses better than I do.
Rama is leaving Chitrakuta. Too many people from Ayodhya come here now, and the memories hurt. He will go south, into the Dandaka forest.
The teacher says the next book is a dark one. Be brave, {player}.
So ends the second book, the Book of Ayodhya.

onWin.objective: Step into the Dandaka forest to begin Book 3.

cmds.say: Wait, {player}! Before you go on, talk to me.
The shrine by the teacher's hut is open to all travellers. Face it and press A to rest or recite.
Pilgrims come to Chitrakuta from far away. I sell them what the forest gives.
Behind the tall grass, a chest of forest roots has been left for travellers.
You found 2 bundles of roots.
